cells.gaps: The newest dated facts (ESCWA's 2025 survey, DJI-003 to DJI-005, held as an ingest note and not as the passage) say local offices hold no electronic records of births or deaths, which disagrees with the city's 2024 account of SIGEC; no row dated to the as-at says any office outside Djibouti-Ville enters digitally, none gives a national count of offices, and SIGEC is not said to be held in a national register. No plan is stated, nothing is held for the last twelve months, and no row shows a birth registration issuing the NNI in practice, so identity integrated is not set; no admissible row names rural offices, so rural gap is not set.
cells.note: SIGEC has entered births and deaths at nine civil-status sites since 2011, all of them in Djibouti-Ville, which is the ladder's system running in the capital only. Stage 3 needs it live in local offices beyond the capital, and the 2025 survey says the opposite.
